item.title: Re: A SCP idea I have
item.content:encoded:
Hey there mrcali, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am not an official reviewer (but I am a flight officer), so take everything I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Crit +
- Close Crit -

Unfortunately, I don't see very much promise in your concept here. The whole thing boils down to 'dummy kills people', and while this may have been acceptable in Series I, expectations have changed. In Series VI, people expect a strong narrative to go along with anomalies (taking a cliche and twisting it is a good example, or just having a great story1). Here, I see no narrative whatsoever other than people dying and nothing interesting happening.

To sum up, your concept is a 'generic murder monster'. It's an anomaly that kills things, with no narrative, no backstory, nothing, to support it. Sometimes these work (they're a lot rarer now, but they were accepted in Series I), but they almost always don't. I'd recommend three things:

1. Heavily reworking this idea (i.e. creating a story behind it, maybe changing the anomaly itself a bit). PM me if you change this, I'll take another look (make sure to link this thread, I don't want to have to sift through the forum to find it).
2. Checking out the Guide Hub for some great articles on ideation and story-ing!
3. Consider contacting someone from the Butterfly Squad after you've reworked this concept, because their advice would be the same as mine as this idea stands currently.


Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!
Footnotes
1. I know this is Series IV, but this one was published very recently.

item.title: Another Day for the (Logistics Department)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Tale

Genre (Optional): Horror, Comedy, Action,

Page Layout (Optional): N/A

Elevator Pitch: Courier Gabriel travels to deliver an unknown SCP to Site-19 with complications along the way.

Central Narrative: Gabriel starts off loading the SCP into his delivery truck, noting not to ask questions on what's inside. Everything goes smoothly (agents with him), until they are attacked by an unknown GOI. The agents are lost or killed and Gabriel must finish this one-day delivery with guns pointed at him in every direction.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: No one has really written about the Logistics Department. I hope to start with these guys and do a series of each department, small and big. All of them will have a tad of workplace comedy, danger, and horror to whatever they're dealing with. It's Ironic how "Another Day" in the Foundation can usually mean life or death, no matter who you are.

Additional Notes: As me anything, I'll answer. I always love to hear a good crit about how to improve. Be blunt. Bash as hard as you can. You'll find I have a thick skull.

Navarro mumbled, violently shaking as he was helped to his feet a wink, the two agents watching as the worn down husk that was Vincent Anderson stumbled onto the stage.

I can not for the life of me figure out what "a wink" is doing in this sentence.

“But the company still exists. Phineas has probably taken over by now. Lop off one head and have another two grow back in its place.”

Oh god I am a sucker for thematic call-backs, and this is especially potent given that Phineas was the one who said that line. Absolutely perfect.

And oh-ho-ho damn, this was a banger of a series ender. Anderson may have "escaped" (not really), but the dynamic is quite different now, isn't it? I wonder how long he can keep control of the company before the rest of everyone decides its time he be overthrown. I mean, he can't just stay top-dog while at all times being at risk of dying or otherwise losing connection to his Saker… right? Intriguing as hell.

item.title: Re: SCP Mermaids of the Midnight Zone
item.content:encoded:
Was asked to take a look at this. I've got a kind of list of items I want to go over, moving from small to big, if you'll bear with me.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-X instances are believed to operate globally.

This seems unlikely to me. How does this thing adapt to different sections of the oceans like that?

In addition, all possess an exceptionally long illicium capable of extending at least 100m, and terminating into a realistic and anatomically accurate body of a human female, connected at the base of the skull.

These human lures act as a direct extension of SCP-X, showing them to possess corresponding intellect and the ability to speak.

Honestly, I'd prefer if the process here were a little more imperfect, like the lure has the general shape of a woman but in daylight it's obviously some kind of growth, or their capacity for speak and intellect is rudimentary at best. It just kinda grounds the idea, I think.

Due to SCP-X’s anomalous abilities, all tank maintenance, feedings, tests, and interviews are to be conducted solely by biologically female staff.
…
These effects are greatly amplified in biologically male individuals.

I do not think the phrase "biologically female/male" in an SCP has ever resulted in anything good. The fixation on biology isn't particularly necessary in the context of what you're doing, anyways, and adding a compulsive effect to amplify victim's desire to have sex with the fish comes with its own host of problems.

Yes, we were attacked by a madman at knifepoint.

This whole thing is a significant amount of information pushed into a small space — why not create an addendum separate from the description to convey this in a more natural manner?

Overall it's got the general shape of an article that I'd like — it's short and it's got a little twist of expectations at the end — but I feel like the way you're communicating that twist lacks a level of nuance. Having the fish state their motivations is a bit of an anticlimax. In addition I can't really develop sympathy for the SCP since I get its motivations, but it's still manufacturing victims' desire to breed and overriding their consent. I feel like you're trying to get me to realize that these fish are just lonely but I'm not convinced.

item.content:encoded:
SCP-5914 is a soulless and non-corporeal entity that takes the forms of any individuals . While not doing its "job," the subject would take the form of a dark figure that displays an unknown type of dark matter. It is approximately 171 centimeters (cm), or 5 feet and 7.5 inches, with luminescent red eyes5. The entity claims that it exists in a place so-called as "The Barreplex"6 that existed in an unknown multi-dimensional location shows no signs of hostility, is capable of speech and understands all sorts of human languages. However, it has a very disrespectful/vulgar, and immature attitude.

Deleted at -23 and three votes.

SCP-5446 or ‘Alex’ appears to be a teenage ███████████ female aged around 14-17, SCP-5446’s appearance is normal from the neck down, but her face appears to be ‘censored’ within all forms of visual contact, this includes through the naked eye and through any sort of photography or videography.

Deleted at -18 and three votes.

SCP-5311 is an unidentified, partially-sentient “creature” that remains in constant confinement to the interiors of lengths of pipe—almost exclusively the plumbing of residential housing (pre-containment). It’s suspected to have remained dormant in the pipes of an unknown location until its accidental discovery, estimated to have been in ██ of the year 20█.

Deleted at -13 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

Scorpion451

+ show block
– hide block

The core idea here is definitely viable. Classic vanilla killer monsters are hard to pull off, but the anomaly is a good one to carry something like that. Ditch the targeting of people who know about it and the sound-trigger thing; this thing only needs the one party trick. It's a solid one.

I'm just going to do a rough breakdown here, if you take this to the forums for an overhaul and second try (and you should) PM me and I'll do a more in-depth one. I'm being a little blunt here because I think this is a strong idea but it will only work with a total overhaul.

The surface problems are tone breaks and bad formatting - scare italics in the Containment procedures, overdramatic statements of how dangerous it is, directly addressing the reader, hard-to-read paragraph organization… lots of little things that draft critique can help you address.

More than that though, you're totally missing the mark on what makes this thing a good monster, and how to present it. There's a lot here telling us we should be afraid of this thing, and not nearly enough showing us any of it. Tied into that, you also show your cards way, way too early, especially with regard to the strongest parts of this.

For instance, Don't beat us over the head with everything that qualifies as a pipe immediately in the containment procedures. Keep it subtle, just say it has to be kept x meters from tube-like structures or objects, and describe how it moves between pipes and manipulates the flow of things through them. And then let it click into place when the containment team points a gun at it. You can do the same with containment breaches demonstrating the endless series of things which can be considered tubes. There's potential for this thing to be scary as hell, it just needs to be used right.

Fragmented Memory 1289

Hmm. This place looks cozy.

Hey! Who are you? This is a restricted server.

Oh, a new friend! Hi! I'm Cubie. I am new around these parts. What's your name?

Deleted at -13 and three votes.

item.title: Re: 'Baby-Aid' - Seeking feedback and Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Asked to take a look at this again.

The Foundation quickly tracks them down, finding that various smaller groups are in possession of these devices and have been exploiting the enhanced children for some time, with one particular incident being the usage of a man born with an anomalous power unit in his torso to power a weapons production facility.

So I'm not sure I can understand the connective tissue here. Even if a group of civilians were aware of the object's properties, how would that result in the exploitation that you're describing? It seems like a drastic jump.

I like the direction you're going, but I feel like you're lacking a central theme to all this. The baby-making machine seems entirely disconnected from the narrative about military operations against grassroots civilian groups. Maybe you could focus in on what the lives of these cyborgs are like a little more, use the anomaly as a stand-in for the traumas of the circumstances under which we're born, have the Foundation spy on a group therapy session where one of these adult instances is venting. There's some emotional work you could do there.

item.title: Re: The Mirror [SEEKING GREENLIGHT]
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello! Not an official reviewer, but I can still read and give my thoughts.
So, I find this idea draft kinda… confusing? I'll elaborate.
What I mostly have reading this are a few questions. Mostly things I either didn't get or that I want a bit more insight in.

The first question is, why does the mirror do all this? Or better put, what is the intended function of the mirror? Ok, balance, copies, makes sense so far. But why emotions? Why the black substance?
To add to that, why was it created in the first place? What was the aim of the creator? Was there a creator?

Which leads me to the second question- is the mirror sentient? You mention it 'being asked' things, so I guess it is, but then you never really specify why or how a sentient mirror came to be a thing. I think you could explore this side of the anomaly.

Next, just what is this 'great equality'? Why do the creations disappear after two days if their counterpart is killed? (I assume they disappear at least).

All in all, this draft just left me… really confused. Again, I am not a critter, nor am I anyone with authority of any kind. But I think this idea lacks a… thread? I dunno. A narrative? Something to make it so all the elements you list form a story and add up to something. So far, this looks like a kinda mysterious and ancient 'thing that does a thing' with secret reasons for doing so.

Then again, it might be that I just did not understand anything, which is why I asked all the questions I did. If that's the case, by all means, feel free and encouraged to correct me!

item.title: Re: The ANTECHAMBER: SCP seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Again, my main issue here is that this seems like a flat retelling of other ideas about Hell. Its conceptual nature and the manner of the punishments don't seem to innovate anything beyond things that your audience has already read or seen about Hell — what makes your vision special?

Additionally your narrative seems less linear and more obsessed with the environment's atmosphere, which usually only works for an SCP if the environment is something novel. If there are explorations of Hell, what do they uncover? What do they add to the article?

A dead spy who had information the Foundation needed was a good motive for it to start using this SCP. Is there a problem in using the Insurgency?

It just seems odd to reference the GOI when they're not involved with the story.

P.S.: Is MTF Psi-8 "Silencers" the right group for this SCP?

Not likely. Silencers deal with ghosts on earth and sending them to their afterlives, and aren't very combat-heavy.

item.title: Re: Pataphysical Containment Site
item.content:encoded:
I'm relatively new here, but I'll try to provide some feedback:

+ Feedback
- Close

Firstly, is the site pataphysical or noospherical? The site described seems to be located in the noosphere or infosphere and would presumably be used to contain memetic and infohazardous entities such as SCP-3002 and SCP-2439. Conversely, pataphysics is strongly tied to the nature of narratives and a pataphysical containment site would contain entities like SCP-423 and SCP-3167. Such a site would likely be tied to operation-overmeta.

Secondly, why must the site be staffed entirely by machines? There are several MTF's within the Foundation that are capable of dealing with informational entities, Omega-0 and Omicron-Rho being the most prominent. Is the site somehow hazardous to such personnel. If so why?

Lastly, I don't see why brain have to be those of reality benders and other anomalies. The foundation has used those before but the proposed site is a noospherical construct within a simulation. It would be far more practical for the foundation to use the brains of agents train for said duty. On a side note, how would 'perceiving' the anomalies help contain them? Do you mean that by 'perceiving' the anomalies the brains can generate suitable containment cells for them?

That being said, I like that concept and hope you can pull it off. I look forward to seeing so SCP's set at this new site.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Pataphysical Containment Site

Appreciate the kind words. I know where the people who don't like it are coming from; they're seeing the end-of-the-world scenarios, the people reacting, the deeper implications, and imagining the stories those elements could support, and not seeing any of that reflected here. But yes, really I was just trying for enough of a framework to support that sudden jolt, and the fridge horror. That way this file is really just the end point of any timeline-destroying narratives you can think of; it's actually the end point of a few timeline-destroying narratives I'm eventually going to post as tales. I didn't think it needed its own dedicated, specific narrative to work, and for two thirds of the readers, it looks like it doesn't. About what I expected.

I agree with the thing about the discussion page; I just did another skip with researcher annotations, SCP-5866, which handles the drafting process very differently. I always intended to do it that way, because that one actually has a narrative in the annotations. This one, I wanted to keep them out of the way for visual clarity.

I'm very glad it worked for you in each case, and thanks!

item.title: Re: June the 31st
item.content:encoded:
It's a great idea but there are a lot of questions here.

Good. Questions help deepen things. Answeres below:

+ show block
– hide block

It just feels like it is being done to isolate The Foundation and that needs to be explained.

It is meant to isolate the Foundation. This whole SCP is meant to make the Foundation feel left out and make them question what they have lost by becoming a part of this scary, bizarre world. I'll explain it like this:

This SCP is to do with our habitation of our own lives. On June the 31st, all of humanity have one day in which they inhabit their lives completely. This means they achieve a kind of wholeness within their minds. They don't worry about what's coming or going, or think about how they are perceived or judged. They are simply in the moment. Think of it like this. How much of our lives do we actually inhabiting. We work, we sleep, we wonder, we worry and we think. And we try and give that meaning, which suggested some kind of dissatisfaction. But on this one day, humanity experience a state of existence free of meaning and instead are just being. A bit like Nirvana in Buddhism but instead of separating themselves from their lives, they emerce themselves in it. Taking ever part of their existence into their minds1.

Now to add the element of the Foundation to this SCP. The Foundation regularly deal with things that are outside the norm. Be it a toaster that has to be referred in the first person, a colossal sea serpant or an actual god. Because fo this, I'd imagine it's incredibly difficult for anyone who is a part of The Foundation to separate themselves from this Fantastic2 world and focus on their short, slightly-blasé lives. They're like Rick from Rick and Morty. They've gained knowledge, power and perception but have had to abandon the simple comforts of everyday life. The Foundation can't partake in this SCP because they can't see and understand the world as they did before.

Why do people not notice the missing day?

If your talking like mathematically or scientifically, The Foundation deal with that. Twigging a few number and word here and their should be hard.

If your talking about the fact people forget the SCP, they forget because is will keep them sane. You experience a mode of being that is nigh-impossible to achieve in everyday. How would you feel if you suddenly returned to a strife filled, noisy, tedious life. Pretty bummed out and angry I'm guessing. And that's why they forget. Now you could ask, "Then what's the point of this SCP at all?". My answer is, I don't know really. I think it's to keep the human race just sane and comfortable enough to keep going. To continue on with their lives without breaking down, going mad and screaming. This SCP is helping humanity, not hurting it.

Heck, why not other individuals?

It is perfectly possible that other individuals are like the Foundation and don't experience this SCP. But I'd argue this is very rare as in order for you not to experience this SCP, your perception of the world has had to change significantly. Other organisations like The Church of the Broken God, Parawatch or The Horizon Initiative may also be exempt from this SCP but I don't really care about them. In this SCP, the only parties in focus are The Foundation and the rest of mankind.

What happens to the rest of the world? Do birds freeze, or what about rivers and currents?

No, nothing freezes or stops. The rest of the world continues as if it was a normal day. I must note that on this day, it's not like all sunny and jolly, like a children's book. The environment doesn't change during this SCP. Only people's attitude, outlook, perception and memories.

And keep in mind that there are people giving birth, suffering from imminent death, and any number of other medical conditions.

That changes nothing. It doesn't matter whether they're in pain or in pleasure. What matters is their perception and focus of it.

Footnotes
1. It may help to read up on something called the "Wash Your Bowl" Zen Koan
2. Fantastic as in le fantastique

item.title: Re: A SCP idea I have
item.content:encoded:
This is a pretty solid idea, but the biggest issue to me is the second form of attack, which is obviously similar to 173. Even if you came up with the idea on your own, I doubt the forum would believe it, and it would probably get less recognition than deserved based on the similarity alone. Other than that, I feel it's a novel idea with the first method of killing. I personally would add some reason for killing, like maybe it needs to feed, but if you want to keep it mysterious, that's fine. I also definitely agree with Slate's criticism, the second method feels less harrowing than the first, and while immediate death is scary, I feel insanity-driven suicide is a far worse fate. You should also specify whether it's an image of the thing or directly viewing it that causes the effects, and if an image won't induce them, I would include a picture of it.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: A SCP idea I have

After reading and re-reading I think what this article needs is for you to tackle on it a psychological profile.

Just make a final note of a Foundation analysis team going on about the info they gleaned from the documents. How they piece things in a way to develop better predictors on expected behaviour, future strategies and a map of associates for GAW.

That way you'll make the documents into something that have value to the Foundation and a reason to be in the article.

I love GAW, but in my headcanon they're a valuable source of involuntary information because they're particularly easy to watch, but too hard to actually caught for it to pay off the effort.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Two standard SCP pages, one outdated for the zone with its discovery and test logs and one for the anomalous human.

Elevator Pitch: The Foundations discovers an area that negates anomalous effects and memories or instructions relating to the anomalous, making them try a more indirect approach to learn about the anomaly which would lead to them to discover that it is caused unknowingly by a human with interest in the supernatural.

Central Narrative: The Foundation discovers an area capable of overriding any anomalous effect, records, or memories related to anomalies or groups of interest after they lose contact with an operative who had remained in the area and find him days later with no memories of his mission or any event related to the Foundation. When investigating the area, other operatives and equipment end up being affected, at which point the Foundation makes the first designation and prepares to investigate in greater depth only to find that all orders or influence are lost in the area, preventing the evacuation of the city ​​or direct communication with its inhabitants while they are inside; limiting himself to observing the area from afar, interviewing anyone leaving the city and determining the boundaries of the area.
During the course of the investigation, the Foundation determines the limits of this anomaly, noting that it varies its position with the passage of time but always maintains the same size, which ends up revealing the person to whom the area is connected. Due to the restrictions given by the anomaly, the Foundation uses his online presence, records, and surveillance to learn about the SCP, discovering his interest in the supernatural.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The research on the limits of the anomaly through unusual means by the Foundation and the discovery of the human cause and its implications.

Additional Notes: I want some advice on how to make the most of the build-up to finish up the article.

item.title: Memory Loss
item.content:encoded:
An SCP that steals memories but doesn't keep them. They're stolen via the SCP looking into a target's eyes & can be stopped by one-way glass/similar stuff. Containment is mostly just the prevention of eye contact. The SCP is humanoid, looks like a young girl, has no memories of anything before containment & has trouble forming new memories (although it's not impossible, just takes repetitive exposure.)

I think you should stick to this idea, but, if you haven't, read some articles from series 6 and the how to write an SCP guide to get your bearings on what will be successful on the site.

Good Luck!

item.title: The Maw
item.content:encoded:
I understand that new authors typically don't write Keter-class scips, but this one just stuck with me, so here I am.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Genre: Mystery, Horror, Action with hints of desperation

Page Layout: Standard format (no ACS)

Elevator Pitch: A solar system that is roughly 2000 Au1 in diameter which is overtaken by a biomass of tremendous proportions. Said biomass is a colonial organism with organic linkages that span the distances between celestial bodies and envelop the planets themselves, effectively turning the entire system into a breeding ground for smaller units of the organism, thus furthering its reach. A central mass which measures ~1.92 million km in diameter engulfs the system's sun, and a large, ovular maw sits atop it.

+Brace Yourself
-You need more time to brace?

[This maw ejects chitinous pods (SCP-XXXX-2) containing small, wormlike entities measuring 45 cm in length (SCP-XXXX-2-A). These pods will crash within a 2 km radius of the coordinates 84"37'02"S 68"32'55"E (Antarctica). Approximately one (1) hour after landing, these worms will "hatch" and burrow into the ice. It is shown that organisms proceed to grow at an indeterminate rate while in these conditions.

When exposed to a human being, SCP-XXXX-2-A will merge with the human's spinal column, controlling synapses and effectively taking the subject over. These instances are aggressive to all forms of life and show resistance to pain. Due to this outcome, a mobile task force (Hammer Down, maybe?) will be stationed within this two kilometer zone, and the trajectories of SCP-XXXX-2 will be tracked. Upon finding the crash zone, MTF will destroy SCP-XXXX-2 and SCP-XXXX-2-A by several means (I've written up a list of these means that will be in the official article.)

The final section of this SCP (I promise), referred to as SCP-XXXX-3, is a triangular portal with equa-distant sides that measures 15 meters tall, located at 84"37'02"S 68"32'55"E. It transports anyone entering to a corresponding portal within SCP-XXXX-1 (the solar system).
]

SCP-XXXX-1 and SCP-XXXX-3 were destroyed by MTF during an exploration, thus re-classifying SCP-XXXX as neutralized.

Central Narrative: The article contains a few exploration logs, which culminates with an MTF force detonating a large device that cause the star to implode, eviscerating all components of the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Several, the first of which will be the title and the "Keter Neutralized" classification. An image too, if I can find one or make my own.

Additional Notes: I was reading a bit about making first time Scips too complex/long. I fully intend to be as concise as possible (no 1730 here, folks). It might also be a bright idea for the struck-through class to be Keter-alterius, due to its alien origins.

Footnotes
1. [The standard unit of measurement used to delineate extremely large distances]

I understand that the subterranean SCP may be a bit overdone. But in the dictatorship people were tortuted in those isolated basements. I would like to trace a parallel with The Stomach, this SCP, meaning that horror is still feeding those victims.

Thanks for your feedback! Have a great day! :D

item.title: A SCP idea I have
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): The standard SCP article format.

Elevator Pitch: The basic idea is a jointed 2 metre tall dummy made of hardwood. When someone views it directly, the person will begin to have visual hallucinations centered around the dummy, This usually drives the viewer to the point of insanity which almost always results in suicide. This is one of 2 methods of killing its victim. The alternative and less likely way of killing is directly attacking its victim, Its theorized that it does this by blurring the vision of any nearby person and/or recording devices that may witness this event. This method is only used when the first does not work.

Central Narrative: The entity was found inside of an abandoned factory with unknown origins, after many people complaining about seeing a "wooden thing" watching them from inside the factory. Paranormal investigators found this interesting and went inside, more than half of them were found dead in their own homes. Foundation researchers went on the case and successfully captured it, with the cost of more than half of the researchers involved die in their offices.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The article will be short and simple, it won't have too much information about the entity leaving a mystery, I am also hoping to add a feeling of dread.

Additional Notes: None.
